about: Scoring definitions read by scripts/score_axes.py. Items are checklist item ids; an entry ending in '*' matches every id with that prefix. Labels are English; the synthesis agent supplies translations in REPORT_DIR/labels.json.

scale.guide_en: A model to learn from. No findings.
Works and reads well. No confirmed major defect.
A few major defects. Good and bad parts in equal measure.
Many major defects. Departures from principles stand out.
One critical defect, or most of it departs from principles.
The concern is not addressed at all.

charts.title: Product quality: can it be used?
charts.subtitle: The nine characteristics of ISO/IEC 25010:2023

axes.label: Functional suitability
axes.question: Does it do what it should?

axes.label: Performance efficiency
axes.question: Does it stay fast and light?

axes.label: Compatibility
axes.question: Does it coexist and exchange data with others?

axes.label: Interaction capability
axes.question: Can people use it without confusion?

axes.label: Reliability
axes.question: Does it hold up when things go wrong?

axes.label: Security
axes.question: Does it protect information?

axes.label: Maintainability
axes.question: Is it easy to change?

axes.label: Flexibility
axes.question: Does it adapt to other environments and scales?

axes.label: Safety
axes.question: Can it harm people or property?

charts.title: Design and construction: is it well engineered?
charts.subtitle: Seven design viewpoints; the design score is computed from all their items

axes.label: Responsibility
axes.question: One job per part, and does the name say it?

axes.label: API and boundaries
axes.question: Can each part be used from its interface alone?

axes.label: Layers and dependencies
axes.question: Are layers and dependency directions right?

axes.label: No duplication
axes.question: Is each job done in one place?

axes.label: State handling
axes.question: Is state held in one place and robust to event order?

axes.label: Tests
axes.question: Is risky behaviour guarded by tests?

axes.label: Simplicity
axes.question: No needless layers, abstractions or complexity?

charts.title: Hard spots: are the error-prone parts right?
charts.subtitle: Ten places where code most often goes wrong

axes.label: Naming
axes.question: Does every name tell what it denotes?

axes.label: Boundaries (off-by-one)
axes.question: Are ranges, indexes and edge values right?

axes.label: Caches and copies
axes.question: Do copies stay in sync with their source?

axes.label: Ordering
axes.question: Is it right when events come in another order?

axes.label: Efficiency
axes.question: Is heavy work done in the right complexity class?

axes.label: Error paths and clean-up
axes.question: Does it stop, report and clean up when something fails?

axes.label: String boundaries
axes.question: Is text encoded where it enters another language?

axes.label: Numbers and units
axes.question: Overflow, rounding, floating point, units?

axes.label: Time and dates
axes.question: Clocks, time zones, daylight saving, calendars?

axes.label: Sharing and mutability
axes.question: Is shared data protected from unexpected changes?
